content:
ida: Hey team — Enterprise customer (AcmeCo) reporting 403 on the Console Billing tab when using our delegated service token. They were fine yesterday.
ida: Context: they use a partner integration that creates delegated tokens with our /v1/tokens API (service tokens, not user keys). After we flipped the new auth-proxy last night some of their flows started getting Forbidden.
ida: Error seen in browser console when clicking Billing -> '403 Forbidden: insufficient_scope' and UI shows no billing CTA. Customer insists their service token has project-admin role.
ida: Quick repro steps they gave: create delegated token via partner, login to Console as a regular org user, switch to project -> click Billing.
samir: Thanks Ida. Do we have a token id or example header from their requests? Any recent token rotations?
support-bot: Audit log (excerpt):
```
{ "event": "token.created", "token_id": "tok_prtn_8f3b", "scopes": ["project:read","project:deploy"], "created_by": "partner-acme-integ" }
{ "event": "proxy.migration", "time": "2025-11-02T03:08:12Z", "note": "default delegated scopes sanitized" }
```
samir: That snippet shows scopes don't include project:billing or project:admin. If the token was created before but rehydrated by proxy, it might have had scopes trimmed during migration.
ida: The customer claims the token used to allow billing access. They sent a screenshot of the token metadata in their partner UI which says role=project-admin.
alex: Paging auth team — there was a migration change that normalizes delegated tokens and drops any scope we don't explicitly list in the allowlist. Billing-related scopes were unintentionally omitted from the new allowlist for delegated tokens.
jordan: Confirming — the auth-proxy now maps role->scopes using a compact table. During the roll we only populated read/deploy for external delegated tokens. Admin/billing scopes remained reserved for user-issued tokens. That's the mismatch.
samir: Can we repro internally? If we mint a delegated token with role=project-admin via partner mock and hit the billing endpoint, do we see 403 with insufficient_scope?
jordan: Yes. Quick curl reproduction: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_prtn_8f3b" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Delegation: partner-acme" \
  https://console.redwood.example/api/v1/projects/acme-prod/billing

# Response: 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope","required":"project:billing"}
```
ida: Customer is blocked — they need billing toggle to update invoices. They asked for a hotfix or workaround.
alex: Short-term workaround: issue a user-scoped admin token (org admin) and use that when performing billing actions via Console. Not ideal. Medium-term: add billing/project-admin scopes back to delegated-token allowlist and roll a patch to auth-proxy.
jordan: I'll open a patch PR to restore mapping for delegated tokens and add an integration test so role=project-admin -> scopes include project:billing. ETA ~ 3 hours for rollout to staging, ~6 hours to prod if no regressions.
samir: For support playbook: 1) Confirm token id and partner. 2) If customer can create a user-scoped admin token, guide them to use it for billing. 3) If not, offer to create a temporary support token scoped to project:billing for them (audit logged).
ida: I'll relay that to AcmeCo and request the token id. Also will ask if they want us to create a temporary support token.
alex: I'll add a postmortem note to eng-ops once fix is merged.
ida: Thanks — looping in customer now. :pray:
